item.title: 'Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting': World Cup-winner sends strong message on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
item.description: NEW DELHI: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already delivered several remarkable batting performances. But his stunning innings against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars could well be the most special of them all. The youngster went after the bowlers from the start and completely dominated the opposition attack. Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus. Many former cricketers and experts have backed the youngster for a regular place in India's T20I team. However, his latest knock also underlined his ability to make an impact in the 50-over format. Former India captain and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth feels the team management must take bold decisions to give Sooryavanshi a bigger role in Indian cricket. Srikkanth questions Gambhir's approach Sooryavanshi has featured in 10 T20Is for India but is yet to cement his place in the playing XI. With the full-strength team available, Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson have been preferred as openers. Srikkanth feels the youngster is not getting enough opportunities despite his impressive performances. He also had a strong message for India head coach Gautam Gambhir. "We need to make some strong moves. Vaibhav was made Bihar captain right away. He was the vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy; him and Ishan (Kishan) won the title. He has been promoted to that level. Gautam is just keeping deaf ears," Srikkanth said, speaking on his YouTube channel. "The team management is playing one game, saying he has to be groomed, and not giving him chances. This guy, on the other hand, is playing his own game. You say it is not in your hands and all of that. Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting. No one can hit like this. Just look at this," he added. 'This is another level' Srikkanth was left stunned by the variety of shots Sooryavanshi played during his remarkable innings. He also praised the youngster's power and timing, saying he had rarely seen anything like it. "What is this? Have you seen anyone hitting the ball like this? Look at the shots he has played. He has his shots everywhere in all ranges. This is another level. This does not happen in book cricket either. I have never seen these kinds of shots. Who is this guy? Which generation is he from? Where does he get so much power and sense of timing?" he further said. Srikkanth also compared the 15-year-old's batting to that of some of the biggest hitters in the game, including AB de Villiers and Chris Gayle. "I have not seen anyone playing like this in a team. Even (AB) De Villiers and (Chris) Gayle did not play like this," Srikkanth concluded. 136184442

item.title: Bearman to continue with Haas in 2027
item.description: In 2025, Oliver Bearman outscored his team-mate Estaban Ocon by three points. This season, he scored three times the points of Ocon before the Frenchman was dropped during the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend [Getty Images] Britain's Oliver Bearman will continue to race for the Haas team in Formula 1 in 2027. The US-based team announced the 21-year-old's new deal on Thursday, at the start of the Qatar Grand Prix weekend. It marks Bearman's third full season with Haas, for whom he first raced for two one-off events in 2024 before becoming a full-time driver in 2025. The announcement ends a protracted negotiation period in which Bearman's management were seeking reassurances about his future from Ferrari. Bearman is a member of the Italian team's driver academy and has ambitions to race for Ferrari in the future. It was not immediately clear what reassurances Bearman had been given about his future by Ferrari. Is Hamilton and Leclerc's Ferrari partnership sustainable? F1 Q&A Camara to continue with Haas for final two races Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us. "We've seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. "He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward." Bearman added: "It's no secret that I'm delighted to be continuing with Haas into 2027. "This team has played an integral role in my development, and I've felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here. "We've got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I'm excited to lead that work, building on what we've achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business." Bearman will be partnered at Haas next season with Brazilian Rafael Camara, who is also a member of the Ferrari driver academy. Camara has started racing for Haas at the end of this season, following the team's sacking of Frenchman Esteban Ocon midway through the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend. Bearman's concerns about his future had been rooted in the fact that there might not be a seat available at Ferrari for some considerable time. Charles Leclerc is on a long-term contract there, and while Lewis Hamilton's deal is believed to end after 2027, the seven-time champion is keen to continue in F1 for a number more years. Bearman, who said at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, that he was "quite disappointed" his new contract had not yet been sorted so late in the season, is believed to have been exploring his options. His management is said to have been asking Ferrari for reassurances about his future, either about the possibility of racing for the main team, or if that is not an option, being allowed to pursue a career at a more competitive team than Haas. item.title: Schalke 04’s Loris Karius plays coy on Bayern Munich transfer links
item.description: Photo by Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty Images | Getty Images Loris Karius’s career hit a downward spiral following his 2017/18 Champions League Final mishap with Liverpool. After losing confidence, he had a two-year loan spell at Beşiktaş, followed by stints at Union Berlin, Newcastle United, and a return to Liverpool. Eventually, Karius landed at 2. Bundesliga side Schalke 04, where he rebuilt his confidence. Last season, he helped Die Königsblauen capture the 2. Bundesliga title and earn promotion back to Germany’s top flight for the first time since the 2022/23 season. Now, the German shot-stopper is putting together a strong campaign with Schalke—and has caught Bayern Munich’s attention. The rumors linking Karius to Bavaria caught many off guard, including the goalkeeper himself. “I heard about it just like you did,” Karius said (as reported by @iMiaSanMia ). “It’s not my place to comment on rumors, and this isn’t the right occasion for that either. I haven’t spoken to anyone. My day-to-day work here is demanding enough as it is. I feel very comfortable at Schalke and really enjoy playing here. We have a lot to look forward to in the coming weeks, so my full focus is on that.” Karius m ay not know much about Bayern’s interest right now, though he’ll have plenty to think about if Die Rekordmeister decides he’s the right veteran option to back up Jonas Urbig next season. item.title: Cristian Chivu praises Inter's mentality after crucial Champions League victory over Stuttgart
item.description: FBL-C1-EUR-FEYENOORD-INTER MILAN - AFP Inter Milan manager Cristian Chivu has praised his side's defensive discipline and mental resilience following their crucial 2-0 victory over VfB Stuttgart at San Siro. The Nerazzurri secured the three points through a Petar Sucic penalty and a late strike from Lautaro Martinez to move up the Champions League table. Nerazzurri find defensive resolve at San Siro Inter successfully navigated a high-pressure European night on Wednesday, securing a win against Stuttgart that alleviates the sting of their recent domestic struggles. After suffering through a chaotic 4-4 draw with Atalanta in which they squandered a two-goal lead, the Italian giants knew they needed a clinical performance to leapfrog their German opponents in the league phase standings. The breakthrough arrived via a penalty converted by Petar Sucic following a handball, before Lautaro Martinez emerged from the bench to seal the victory. While the performance wasn't always fluid, the ability to grind out a result against a dangerous Stuttgart outfit suggests the squad has learned from their recent defensive lapses. "We relied on mentality, organisation, intensity, accepting that Champions League games are not easy, that you cannot dominate them from start to finish,” the Inter boss explained to Sky Sport Italia . He acknowledged that the team had to be patient, adding: "At times you need to stay in the match, try to make the most of opposition errors, but also try to be proactive when possible. The moments of a match are important and you need to read them." Chivu defends tactical adjustments Despite the win, questions remain regarding Inter's tendency to drop their intensity during certain phases of play. Chivu addressed these concerns by pointing out that his team was prepared to suffer when Stuttgart pushed forward early on. item.title: Viktor Gyokeres warns Arsenal not to ‘waste energy’ on Man City sanctions as Gunners eye back-to-back titles
item.description: Arsenal FC v Borussia Dortmund - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Viktor Gyokeres has issued a firm rallying cry to his Arsenal teammates, insisting the club will not waste a single second of focus on Manchester City’s ongoing legal battles. The Swedish international is determined to secure consecutive Premier League titles and believes the Gunners are now fully accustomed to the pressure of being frontrunners. Arsenal host struggling City amid legal uncertainty Emirates Stadium hosts a pivotal Premier League showdown on Sunday as Arsenal face Manchester City for the first time since September's financial regulations verdict. City were found guilty of serious breaches but have lodged an appeal , leaving potential sanctions unresolved and the title race in limbo. Since that ruling, Enzo Maresca's side have suffered a sharp slump. They have claimed just one victory across their last seven matches in all competitions, collecting a single point from a possible 12 in the league. Gyokeres dismisses off-pitch noise and respects City's quality Asked whether potential sanctions against City could alter the title race, Gyokeres brushed off the off-field drama: "No. It is what it is. We are focused on the game on Sunday. We can't control that. It has nothing to do with us. So, we don't put any energy into that." Despite City's poor run of form, the Sweden international warned against underestimating Sunday's visitors. "They still have a very good squad and very good players," Gyokeres continued. "Sometimes, you may have a period where you don't get the results all the time - which is normal for any club. It is going to be a difficult game on Sunday. But it is always fun with big games. It is going to be good." Arteta's champions chase historic consecutive crowns Mikel Arteta's side sit six points clear of last season's runners-up as clear favourites to retain the Premier League crown for the first time in Arsenal's history. Fresh from scoring in Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund , Gyokeres is pushing to start and emphasised their title hunger. "We always want to win titles and we know how tough it is in the Premier League with the games and the teams," he said. "But we have an amazing squad, amazing players, so that's the aim. item.title: Burnley 0-2 Birmingham City - fans' verdict
item.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Birmingham City won 2-0 at Burnley on Wednesday to make it an EFL record 24 home games without a win for the Clarets while Blues closed the gap at the top of the Championship. Here are some of your comments: Clarets fans Lynne: Tragic. No desire to push forward or take responsibility in front of goal. The fans are despondent as are the players. It's so sad to watch. Brian : The worst performance ever. Many will not renew season tickets until Pace has gone. Steve : Going backwards. Losing possession has been a problem all season, as has schoolboy defending. We are so so slow building attacks it's ridiculous. It's like we allow any team to get back in shape before we attack. Kyle Walker has been terrible and even Amdouni, who has been loved by the fans, has had stinkers in the last two games. I can see us going down again and the owners have created all this. They should resign as a board and sell up and go back to the US. Darren : Woeful, no fight in any of them. We are staring at League One football without a doubt. Mark : We were shocking. Our defence is about as useful as a chocolate fireguard. Vardy should have started, he'd have gotten on the end of Ramazani's crosses and balls into the box. It was a very lacklustre performance. On these performances we're down. Blues fans Phil : A routine win against a very poor team. In Blues' favour it's not the easiest place to visit on a cold winter evening. Gary : Good start but some sloppy play meant we needed Beadle to be on top form. Fry and Neumann excellent, Klarer has a rival for his place now, some puzzling substitutions from Davies. David : It's wins like this that win Championships and promotions. They build confidence which is so important. Daniel : Very professional performance, could have been more comfortable. Burnley had very good possession but no end product. Looking forward to upcoming games, real battle at the top now, bring it on. John : This win looks good but we could easily have lost if Burnley had taken their chances. In my opinion we were quite lucky in some ways.

item.title: Experienced Real Madrid defender misses another chance to impress Jose Mourinho
item.description: Experienced Real Madrid defender misses another chance to impress Jose Mourinho During the early phase of the campaign, Real Madrid fans were yearning for the return of Eder Militao from injury. The Brazilian international is widely considered the de facto leader of the Real Madrid defence, due to his experience and the consistency he has shown in the past. After yet another long injury spell, Militao eventually received the medical clearance earlier in the season, but his road to the first team has been much more difficult than expected. Jose Mourinho has been very careful in integrating Militao into the starting eleven, giving him opportunities primarily in Champions League matches. Militao fails yet again Time for Militao to step up his game. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) However, in those limited opportunities, Militao hasn’t really been able to show that he should be Real Madrid’s starting centre-back. Indeed, the Brazilian has featured in both UCL games against AEK Athens and PSV Eindhoven, and he has struggled in both. A start against Militao was an excellent opportunity for Militao to prove himself. But he had a disastrous start to the proceedings and was completely overrun by the speedy PSV frontline. Mourinho eventually made the decision to bench him at half-time. In the two matches Militao has started this season, Real Madrid have conceded three goals and are yet to keep a clean sheet. Konate and Huijsen remain the top choice options Militao’s form has been concerning for Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Militao’s relatively poor performances suggest he is not yet ready to become a first-team regular in the Real Madrid setup. Whether or not that is because of his fitness remains to be seen. But for now, it appears Mourinho has clearly identified Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen as his first-choice options in central defence. Antonio Rudiger is another option for Mourinho. But much like Militao, the German veteran also struggled to keep up with the PSV attack this midweek and was replaced at half-time. This is a sign of a broader issue at Real Madrid, where Mourinho has observed that second-fiddle players have failed to offer the same quality as his first-choice stars. The coming weeks, therefore, could prove to be crucial for Militao as he looks to regain full fitness and provide some strong performances, which in turn may help him push for a regular starting role at the heart of Los Blancos backline.

(Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) Celtic are reportedly keeping tabs on Belarus International goalkeeper Fedor Lapoukhov as Martin O’Neill looks to bolster his options between the sticks. The Belarus international faced Scotland at Hampden last year and has been monitored by Celtic ever since according to reports. It is understood that Celtic’s interest is a more long term one, with a view to a bid next summer as opposed to the upcoming January transfer window. The 23 years old 6ft 3 shot-stopper plays his club football for Bulgarian side CSKA Sofia, and has already amassed 20 caps for the Belarusian national side, and played against Scotland in the World Cup qualifiers last year. Fedor Lapoukhov of Belarus fails to save as Gustav Isaksen of Denmark scores his team’s second goal during the FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifier match between Denmark and Belarus at Parken Stadium on November 15, 2025 in Copenhagen, Denmark. item.title: ESPN’s Desmond Howard Makes His Stance Clear on Alabama’s Controversial Ranking
item.description: Oct. 8, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; ESPN personality Desmond Howard arrives at the Bama Theatre for the red carpet premiere of SABAN, the new ESPN Originals docuseries. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama football remains firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation, but the Crimson Tide’s latest ranking has sparked another debate. ESPN analyst Desmond Howard weighed in Wednesday, Nov. 25, after the selection committee made a significant adjustment to its postseason rankings. The former Heisman Trophy winner did not hide his opinion about where Alabama belongs. Desmond Howard Reacts to Alabama’s Ranking During Wednesday’s edition of ESPN’s “Get Up,” Howard discussed the committee’s decision to move Alabama from No. 3 to No. 6. The Crimson Tide fell behind Texas, Notre Dame and Tennessee despite improving to 9-2 with Saturday’s victory over Chattanooga. However, Howard believes the committee made the correct decision. “I thought they finally got it right,” Howard said. The ESPN analyst questioned why Alabama had remained ahead of teams with stronger victories in previous rankings. In particular, Howard pointed toward Texas and its collection of quality wins. The Longhorns moved to No. 3 after spending recent weeks behind Alabama. Howard Points to a Major Difference Between Alabama and Texas Howard believes the committee should prioritize the quality of each team’s victories when evaluating playoff contenders. Texas has defeated Ohio State, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU this season. Meanwhile, Alabama does not currently own a victory over a team ranked in the committee’s latest top 25. That difference played a significant role in Howard’s assessment. The analyst also questioned why Texas had remained behind Alabama despite its stronger collection of ranked victories. For Howard, the results on the field should carry more weight than a team’s reputation. His comments add another prominent ESPN voice to the debate surrounding Alabama’s playoff résumé. Tennessee Also Moves Ahead of Alabama Texas wasn’t the only SEC program to pass Alabama in Tuesday’s rankings. Tennessee climbed to No. 5, moving one position ahead of the Crimson Tide. The Volunteers defeated Alabama 26-10 earlier this season, giving Tennessee a valuable head-to-head advantage. However, Alabama had remained ahead of Tennessee in previous committee rankings. item.description: Photo: Peter Kneffel/dpa (Photo by Peter Kneffel/picture alliance via Getty Images) “What a week, huh?” “Captain, it’s Wednesday.” Bayern Munich could probably use that exchange as the unofficial motto for the last several d ays. Between the public discussion surrounding J amal Musiala, comments from club leadership, questions about his contract, and now reporting from Sport Bild’s Christian Falk and Julian Agardi (via @iMiaSan Mia ) about Vincent Kompany reassuring players and club employees regarding Musia la’s health, it has been an exhausting news cycle. According to Falk and Agardi, Kompany told his players during a dressing-room team talk that they should have absolutely no concerns about Musiala or his health, assuring them that their teammate is in excellent health and full of energy. Kompany reportedly delivered the same reassurance to several other club employees. The reassurance comes after a week in which Musiala has seemingly become the center of a wider Bayern Munich debate that has extended well beyond football. Comments and crit icism from Jan-Christian Dreesen, Uli Hoeneß, and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge regarding Musiala, his contract, and his situation have helped fuel the perception of a growing divide between the player a nd the club. What might ordinarily be an internal conversation about a player’s development, recovery, contractual future, and expectations has increasingly played out publicly, leaving Musiala at the center of a debate that is difficult to separate from the footballing realities. That is where this entire situation has become particularly uncomfortable. Musiala is not just a contract negotiat ion, a talking point for club executives, or a headline generator. He is a player recovering, trying to get back to his best, and one whose importance to Bayern Munich is difficult to oversta te. Public discourse can easily turn a complicated situation into a perceived confrontation, but that does not necessarily reflect what is happening behind closed doors. Ultimately, though, thi s is about Jamal Musiala’s health. The hope should be that he gets fully healthy, regains his confidence, and returns to the form that made him one of the mo st highly regarded talents in world football. That is what matters most, regardless of the noise, the speculation, or the conversations about who knew what and when. Will he get back to a top level? Is he worth the massive contract? Enjoy: In lieu of an Entertainment Rundown As the podcast listeners know, I’ve been on the road a bit and had no time to watch anything, but there is a topic that needs to be addressed… Manuel Neuer has found himself caught up in yet ano ther controversy, and while the latest discussion surrounding the Bayern Munich captain might change how some people view him personally, it should not change how we evalua te him as a footballer. At some point, though, the squad has to get past t he headlines and conjecture and remember why it is here in the first place: a Champions League tilt vs. LOSC Lille. LOSC Lille is not great, let alone a powerhouse, but it has — at least — had a week not mired in controversy. In addition, while Lille does have some injuries, its front line is mostly intact. The same cannot be said for Bayern Munich, which is limping into the game. At some point, though, the pride wi thin the Bavarians has to show through all of the nonsense going on around the squad. The fight and heart will need to be on full display, and the mentality of a true champion will either be there when the whistle blows or… it won’t. item.title: VCU wins on another clutch game-winner for 2nd game in a row
item.description: MT1USATODAY28561151 VCU wins on another clutch game-winner for 2nd game in a row appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . VCU pulled off another last-minute escape at the Maui Invitational, overcoming Washington 80-78 behind guard Nyk Lewis’ game-winning heroics Wednesday night in Lahaina. Lewis connected on a jumper in the paint with just seconds remaining to complete VCU’s comeback and improve its record to 5-2. The win came a day after guard Blake Harper hit a 45-foot buzzer-beater to give the Rams an 84-81 win over Colorado State. VCU wins it late for a second straight night 🔥 @VCU_Hoops https://t.co/JWvXOxYf6E pic.twitter.com/QsfyH3WrbJ Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) November 26, 2026 VCU trailed by as many as 10 points in the second half against the Huskies but finished the contest with an 8-1 run. Washington appeared to be in control late, holding a 77-72 advantage after forward Nikola Dzepina converted two free throws with 2:47 remaining. However, Harper knocked down four free throws before Lewis added two more, putting the Rams ahead 78-77 with approximately 24 seconds left. Huskies guard Ryan Beasley then made one of his two free-throw attempts to level the score at 78-78 with 12 seconds remaining. Following a timeout, Lewis drove into the lane and converted the decisive jumper. Washington had one final opportunity, but Dzepina’s long-range attempt bounced off the back of the rim as time expired. Forward Torey Alston led VCU with 19 points off the bench, while Harper contributed 17. Junior guards Ahmad Nowell and Brandon Jennings also contributed 13 points apiece. Meanwhile, Dzepina finished with a career-best performance for the Huskies, recording 31 points while shooting 7-of-9 from beyond the arc. LeJuan Watts added 17 points and nine rebounds for Washington, which fell to 5-2. The Huskies held a 42-41 halftime advantage after a first half featuring nine lead changes and six ties. Washington also maintained its advantage throughout the second half until the Rams’ late comeback. Both teams finished shooting 50% from the field. The Huskies connected on 13 of its 23 three-point attempts, compared to VCU’s 8-of-22 performance. Washington also controlled the boards 33-23 but committed 17 turnovers that resulted in 19 points for the Rams. The Huskies went without a made field goal over the final 3:43, allowing VCU to complete another late comeback. Up next, the Rams will return home to face Coppin State on December 3. Winning possession high up the pitch before finishing from Matias Soule's cut-back, the Spanish centre-back helped Gian Piero Gasperini's side end PSG's 100 per cent Champions League start despite goals from Illia Zabarnyi and Ousmane Dembele, with substitute Donyell Malen converting a late penalty after Vitinha's handball. "Everyone knows what the coach does, this is his identity, his style of playing," Hermoso told Sky Sport Italia after collecting UEFA's Player of the Match award. "We defenders get the opportunity to be protagonists, so I am very happy to come to a stadium like this, and see Roma playing in this special way, with no fear. We are on the right track and must keep taking these big steps forward." Training ground drills and Gasperini's squad rotation Gasperini sprang a tactical surprise by leaving Malen, Paulo Dybala and Bryan Cristante on the bench from the start, yet Roma's rotated line-up matched the French giants across 90 minutes. item.description: Europa League: Olympiacos vs. Milan – Probable line-ups and where to watch on TV Ruben Amorim and Milan find themselves in need of points in the Europa League table and are preparing for a tough test away against the unbeaten Olympiacos in Athens on Thursday evening. The Rossoneri have won just one and lost three of their first four matches in the Europa League this season, and will be tasked with taking on Olympiacos, who have three wins and one draw on their record so far this term. ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Lenny Joseph of Ferencvarosi TC scores his team’s second goal under pressure from Mario Gila of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between AC Milan and Ferencvarosi TC at Stadio San Siro on November 05, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Milan were victorious on their return to action over the weekend following the recent international break, putting five past Frosinone in a dominant display that brought goals from Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic. They will be without nine players for Thursday’s clash with Olympiacos, though. Luka Modric, Strahinja Pavlovic, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers, Samuel Chukwueze, Francesco Camarda, David Bartesaghi and Pierro Terracciano are all expected to be unavailable this evening. That means that Amorim is unable to make too many alterations to the side that beat Frosinone over the weekend. Permission Estupinan is set to replace Bartesaghi at left-back, Ardon Jashari could come into the starting XI and Omari Hutchinson could also be introduced to the attack. item.title: How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish?
item.description: How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish? Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night. The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match. That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February. Now that we’re past the halfway mark of the league phase, the 36 Champions League clubs have a strong indication as to where they’re likely to finish, and what more needs to be done to achieve their targets. Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust How many more points do Liverpool need for top-eight finish? At present, Manchester City occupy the final position for automatic passage to the round of 16, with Enzo Maresca’s side on 10 points, averaging two per game. That means the projected points tally required for a top-eight placing is 16, so Liverpool would need to aim for at least four points from their remaining three matches against Porto (home), Inter Milan (away) and Lens (home). The two Anfield fixtures are against teams placed 22nd and 34th respectively, so the Reds would be fully expected to win both of those. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The visit to the San Siro is likely to be much tougher, but LFC beat Inter at the famous venue last season, and a repeat result would probably be enough to guarantee a top-eight finish with one game to spare. That’d give Iraola the luxury of being able to rest key players for the concluding fixture against Lens, which falls between Premier League matches against Manchester United and Everton. Top-eight finish well within reach for Liverpool With Liverpool also still going strong in the Carabao Cup and plausibly making it to a two-legged semi-final in the opening weeks of 2027, any opportunity to rotate the squad in January must be embraced. The picture can obviously change over the final three matchdays, but right now it seems probable that if the Reds beat Porto and get a result away to Inter, they could be effectively or even mathematically assured of a top-eight finish by the time they host Lens. That objective is well within reach for Iraola’s side, and avoiding the play-off round in February is a must.

item.title: Major MLS playoff overhaul confirmed as league axes wild card round and best-of-three series

United - Getty Images Sport Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers. MLS set for major play-off overhaul MLS is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season structure , even as the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs get under way. Beginning with the 2027-28 season, the league will eliminate its short-lived wild card round and scrap the best-of-three first-round format, according to reports from The Guardian . The changes will condense the play-off field to 16 teams. Under the new model, the opening two rounds will be played as two-legged, home-and-away ties, while the semi-finals and final will revert to single-elimination matches hosted by the higher seed. Why the league is scrapping best-of-three Introduced in 2023, the best-of-three opening round has proved ineffective at sustaining drama or rewarding regular-season excellence. Over the past three campaigns, a staggering 35 days elapsed between the end of the regular season and the second round due to the November international break. item.title: Charles Barkley heaps praise on Deni Avdija, Blazers after NBA Cup upset over Spurs
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Charles Barkley heaps praise on Deni Avdija, Blazers after NBA Cup upset over Spurs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Charles Barkley has never been shy about his praise for Deni Avdija. The former NBA player had plenty of praise for the young forward after the Portland Trail Blazers beat the San Antonio Spurs 116-111 in NBA Cup group-stage action on Wednesday night. Barkley also appreciated Portland’s athleticism and offensive firepower after the upset. He then singled out Avdija, praising his aggressive approach and comparing him to former NBA star Drazen Petrovic. “This is a good team, man. They big, they’re athletic, and when you have two guys who can score,” Barkley said. “And that boy Avdija, let me tell you something — he is so aggressive offensively. I love… I said at halftime, Stojaković… not Stojaković, Dražen Petrović — like he reminds me of him. Like he going straight forward, you going to stop him?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “[ Deni Avdija ’s] not afraid of anything, he’s not afraid of the moment.” Charles Barkley is a big fan of Deni Avdija and the Blazers 🗣️ (via @ESPNNBA ) pic.twitter.com/4lQO6BaxK6 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 26, 2026 Barkley added that Avdija isn’t afraid to take shots or make mistakes, even when his attempts aren’t falling. He also questioned the Washington Wizards’ decision to let the forward go. “I’m just trying to figure out why the Wizards let him go. It just goes to show you a lot of these teams don’t know what the hell they’re doing,” Barkley said. Avdija backed up that praise with a strong performance against San Antonio. He finished with 33 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists, while Damian Lillard added 29 points and seven assists to help Portland secure the win. Avdija also delivered the decisive moment and banked in a three-pointer with 37.9 seconds remaining to give the Blazers a five-point cushion. This was not the first time Barkley compared Avdija to Petrovic. During the 2026 NBA playoffs , Barkley made a similar comparison while discussing Avdija’s aggressive scoring mentality. The win tightened the race in West Group C, with Portland, San Antonio, Golden State, and the Los Angeles Lakers all sitting at 2-1 with one game remaining in the group stage. item.title: Exeter not 'the finished article', says boss Taylor
item.description: Matt Taylor has seen his side lose just one of their past 10 games in all competitions - away at League Two leaders Salford City [Shutterstock] Exeter City are "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form, manager Matt Taylor has said. Having been a point above the relegation places at the end of September, Exeter have become one of League Two's in-form teams. They have lost just one of their past 10 matches in all competitions, keeping clean sheets in half of those games. It has seen them rise to eighth in the division and also book an FA Cup second round tie after winning at then League One leaders Huddersfield Town in the first round. "The last 10 games now has been a period of games where we lost one, and that was as good a performance as we've had all season at Salford against a very strong opposition, incredible cup results and good league form," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "So we're going in the right direction, but nowhere near the finished article. "We'll constantly have challenges in-game and in the lead-up to games with the way we are as a group in terms of real depth and experience. "But in terms of the strides and the progress I think individuals have made within the team in that period I'm speaking about, I think you can see players are performing to a better level and with a bigger output and a bigger influence on the game. "I've always said I'll sleep well at night as long as the group is honest with me. "I feel this is a really honest group, but I'm still as excited as ever to see where it could take us in two weeks' time, in two months' time, in two years' time for some of them, but certainly as this season goes deeper seeing where we're at." Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap Taylor impressed with Exeter City's Oldham comeback Exeter host a resurgent Crawley Town on Saturday (12:30 GMT) with the joint-second best home record in League Two. They have conceded just twice in eight games at St James Park, winning five and drawing the other three. It is a record that Taylor is proud of, having won their past four home games. "There's certain records we're really proud of this season: our defensive record, clean sheets, our home record, our home form," added Taylor. "Even more so because it connects the team with the fans. You want a strong home showing. "Very rarely this season do I think our home fans have gone home disappointed or frustrated with what they've seen and that's the majority of our fan base, that's where they get to see us, close to home, less travel involved. "Also, we have to take into account how far opposition teams have to travel down to us, same for us when we go to Oldham and Crawley, all these teams away from home, not just the north but London-based as well. This isn't an easy place to come to but we've got to make sure our energy is in the right place on Saturday." All the latest Exeter City news

item.title: 19 Hillsdale County volleyball athletes earn all-league SCAA-East
item.description: ILLSDALE COUNTY — Hillsdale County volleyball programs dominated the Southern Central Athletic Association East Division postseason honors following the 2026 fall sports season, accounting for all four Dream Team selections and 19 all-conference honorees. Of course there’s plenty to be thankful for, but at a moment like this nothing comes to mind. item.title: Oliver Bearman locks in Haas F1 seat as 2027 grid officially set
item.description: Motorsport photo Oliver Bearman will officially stay at Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season after he and the team finally put pen to paper on a new deal. The American squad announced the renewal on Thursday, meaning the 21-year-old Briton will partner Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara at Haas next season. It means the 2027 grid is now complete ahead of the final two rounds of the 2026 campaign, one in which Bearman has shone with 23 of Haas' 31 points. Team boss Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us. "We’ve seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. "He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward. Ayao Komatsu, Haas Ayao Komatsu, Haas "TGR Haas F1 Team has one of the most exciting driver pairings on the grid, and I look forward to seeing Ollie flourish further with this incredible team." Next season will be Bearman's third, full campaign in F1, although he did make three appearances in 2024 - his debut for Ferrari in Jeddah, before outings in Baku and Sao Paulo for Haas. "It’s no secret that I’m delighted to be continuing with TGR Haas F1 Team into 2027," said Bearman. "This team has played an integral role in my development, and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here. "We’ve got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I’m excited to lead that work, building on what we’ve achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business." Although this news comes late into the season, the Ferrari protege was always going to stay with Haas, which has loaned him from the Scuderia since his rookie year. Oliver Bearman, Haas Oliver Bearman, Haas But as he is entering year three with the American squad, Bearman's camp also wanted assurances about his long-term future - with driving for Ferrari being his ultimate goal. Bearman's camp is also believed to have been looking for a significant pay increase, considering he's become Haas' lead driver after outperforming the now ousted Esteban Ocon . At last week's Las Vegas Grand Prix, Bearman admitted he was "quite disappointed" that "I'm sitting here at round 20 without a contract signed for next year. It's been a strange situation, but we're getting there." He now heads into Qatar this weekend with that new deal ahead of the Abu Dhabi finale, as Haas attempts to hold off Audi in the battle for seventh with three points separating them. item.title: Alejandro Garnacho and the curious case of Aston Villa’s outcast loanees | Ben Fisher
item.description: Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award. He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford. This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He’s more elegant’: Bellingham downplays Zidane comparisons after wondergoal
item.description: Englishman hailed by teammates and manager Mourinho after coming on to completely change Champions League game against PSV Eindhoven “It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo , that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s. “I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally [my goals are] a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either. Continue reading...

item.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to fiasco but issues do not stop there | Osasu Obayiuwana
item.description: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history. As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday , was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute. item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

item.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
item.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, not long after the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to the finals of the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentine Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

item.description: Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says. Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 . “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
